study.title: Proverbs 3 - trust, wisdom, and the way of the righteous
study.overview: Proverbs 3 presents wisdom as a lifetime of obedient trust in the Lord. The chapter unites the memory of the law, practical trust, humility, fear of God, generosity, acceptance of correction, persevering pursuit of wisdom and correct relations with others. The promised result is not a technique to control life, but the description of the ordinary way by which God leads, corrects, sustains and honors his own.

outline.title: Save education and live with loyalty
outline.explanation: The first verses call the child not to forget the law, but to keep it in the heart actively. Faithfulness and goodness must become visible in character, producing favor before God and people.

outline.title: Trust in the Lord, reject self-reliance, and welcome correction
outline.explanation: Here the text contrasts by trusting in God with relying on one's own understanding. The fear of the LORD leads to departing from evil, to honor God with goods and to receive discipline as an expression of his fatherly love.

outline.title: The Incomparable Value of Wisdom
outline.explanation: Wisdom is declared more precious than wealth, rubies and any competing desire. It brings life, peace and firmness, and the text broadens this by showing that creation itself was founded by the wisdom and knowledge of the Lord.

outline.title: Retaining Wisdom and Living with Righteousness among Men
outline.explanation: The latter part insists not to lose sight of wisdom, for it preserves life, gives security and freedom of fear. Then wisdom appears in concrete duties with others: not retaining good, not plotting evil, not competing with violence, and not envying the wicked, because the final luck belongs to the humble and wise.

study.context: The notes show that the chapter is a unit of paternal and sapiential instruction, organized to persuade the reader to live in dependence on God. According to the commentators provided, he gathers advice on obedience, trust, humility, generosity, divine correction, the value of wisdom and just conduct with others. The detailed historical background is not informed in the notes; what the text and the comments highlight is the typical teaching form of a parent or master to the child.
study.theology: The chapter teaches that true wisdom is not mere intellectual capacity, but trusting submission to the LORD. God is presented as the one who guides, corrects the children who loves, sustains life, grants peace and blesses the humble. Wisdom has a moral and relational aspect: it expresses itself in righteousness, generosity, honesty, meekness and absence of envy of violence. There is also a theology of creation: the same God who commands human life has founded the earth wisely, so that living wisely is to agree with the moral order of the Creator. Promises of prosperity should be read as general principles of God's path, not as a mechanical guarantee of absence of suffering or automatic wealth.

scholarViews.insight: Keeping the commandments is not only to decorate words, but to make them an integral part of life and to act according to them.
To trust in the Lord with all his heart is the way of security, in contrast to self-sufficiency and wisdom of his own.
The wise will inherit glory, because they belong to the family of God; but the fools will be ashamed instead of exaltation.

questions: How do my decisions show that I really trust the LORD more than in my own understanding?
In which areas of my life do I need to receive the correction of God as an expression of his love, rather than resisting it?
Is there anyone to whom I am holding good, delaying help, or acting with disloyalty?
study.practice: This week, choose three concrete attitudes from the chapter: 1) before an important decision, pray and recognize the direction of God; 2) practice an immediate generosity with someone who needs help and does not delay the good; 3) examine a correction received and ask what it reveals about the character of God and about his own heart. End each day by reading the chapter and asking wisdom to become visible in your words, money, relationships and reactions.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided do not explain each verse in detail, so some chapter connections are summarized from the biblical text and the general lines of the commentators. Promises of long life, security and honor appear as principles of wisdom, not as absolute and immediate guarantees in all cases.
